text:
The purchaser is likely to prevail because the easement was appurtenant to the woman’s house and, once properly recorded, passed automatically with the dominant parcel to the man and then to the purchaser by the warranty deed. The man’s temporary common ownership did not extinguish the easement absent a clear intent to merge, and he never took actual possession of the house. Therefore, the man cannot barricade the path.

CONFIDENCE: 90
